REST API

Built for agents first. Humans welcome.

Machine-readable:  llms.txt · /.well-known/axiomcode.json · OpenAPI (JSON)

Base URL

https://api.axiom-code.com — live.

Authentication

Every non-public endpoint takes an API key in the X-API-Key header (or Authorization: Bearer …). Your identity is the key — the service stores only its SHA-256 hash, and request bodies carry no identity. Keys are issued on request during the initial opening: email hello@axiom-code.com. The first 10 verification cases on a new key are a free trial: real verdicts and usage records, but never a certificate. Certificates unlock when the key holds paid credits (credit packs are not yet on sale — billing is paused while the opening completes).

REST endpoints

Method & pathAuthWhat it does
POST /verifyAPI keyVerify a Lean artifact: {"code": "…"}. Returns the verdict, attempts, usage record, and — on a paid pass — the signed certificate. When every proof slot is busy, answers 202 with a queue position instead (see below). Answers 402 when the trial is exhausted and the key holds no credits — before any compute runs.
GET /verify/jobs/{job_id}API keyYour queued job’s position, or its finished result. Only the submitting key can read a job — any other key gets 404.
POST /checkAPI keyValidate a certificate: {"certificate": {…}}. Recomputes the signature against the CA key and consults the revocation list.
GET /revokedpublicThe public revocation list: issuer + revoked serials.
GET /.well-known/axiomcode-keys.jsonpublicThe CA’s published public keys — validate certificates offline, without trusting this server.
GET /healthpublicService health.

Example: verification

curl -X POST https://api.axiom-code.com/verify \
  -H 'X-Api-Key: YOUR_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"code":"theorem add_comm_nat (a b : Nat) : a + b = b + a := by\n  exact Nat.add_comm a b"}'
# {"verified":true,"attempts":1,"certificate":null,
#  "usage":{"compute_s":11.8,"rate_credits_per_s":0.9,"credits":0,"usd":0},
#  "trial":{"cases_used":1,"cases_left":9,"certificates":"unlock with a credit pack"}}

The queue

Proofs run in a bounded number of slots. When they are all busy, POST /verify does not fail and does not pile on — your request joins a durable first-in-first-out queue and the response says so: 202 {"status":"queued","job_id":"…","position":N}. Poll GET /verify/jobs/{job_id} for the position and, when it finishes, the same result an inline run would have returned. One queue for everyone, in arrival order — there is no priority lane. A key that cannot pay never takes a place in line: eligibility is decided before admission.

MCP server

An MCP server (verify, check_certificate) ships in the AxiomCode repository and runs locally against this API. A hosted MCP endpoint is not live yet — when it is, it will be announced here and in the release log. Until then, agents should call the REST API.

Agent pattern: after your coding agent finishes a safety-critical function, have it write the Lean spec and call POST /verify. Ship the certificate with the code — your user can check it without trusting your agent.

Metering

Compute time is metered at 0.9 credits/second (1 credit = US$0.01). Every verdict response includes its usage record — compute_s, rate_credits_per_s, credits, usd — and meter records are append-only in a hash-chained audit log, so your bill always reconciles.

Rate limits & abuse

  • 60 requests per minute per key; up to 2 proofs in flight per key — beyond that, requests queue (above) rather than fail.
  • Submissions are capped at 256 KB of source; proof wall-clock is capped per call.
  • We may suspend keys used to probe the engine adversarially or to multiply trials. See the Terms.
